concepts.preferred_label: Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder
concepts.why: The patient's worsening dream enactment behavior, violent episodes during sleep, and yelling multiple times per night are characteristic of RBD.
The patient's initial and repeat polysomnography results demonstrate obstructive sleep apnea with Apnea Hypopnea Index scores of 8.5 and 12.8, respectively.
The patient has a 15-year history of Parkinson disease with a Hoehn and Yahr score of 3, indicating moderate to severe disease.
The patient has a 20-year history of sleep disturbance, which may be related to his Parkinson disease or other underlying conditions.
The patient's severe episode resulting in a head laceration after striking the wall may indicate a traumatic brain injury.
The patient's violent behaviors during sleep, including assault on his wife and self-injurious behaviors, are characteristic of nocturnal aggression.
The patient's emergency department neuroimaging was unremarkable, which may help rule out other underlying conditions.

concepts.preferred_label: Nocturnal Aggression Secondary to Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder
concepts.why: It explains the violent dream enactment behavior despite unremarkable neuroimaging.
